question: A support team wants to build a comprehensive FAQ from a large set of historical customer tickets. Which decomposition technique is most suitable?
options: A) Employ a third-party FAQ generator instead of using Claude.
B) Cluster tickets by topic, generate FAQs per cluster, then merge.
C) Ask Claude to summarize each ticket, then combine into an FAQ.
D) Concatenate all tickets and ask Claude to produce the FAQ.
correct_answers: B) Cluster tickets by topic, generate FAQs per cluster, then merge.
explanations: Incorrect. Employing a third-party generator avoids the decomposition challenge rather than addressing it, and does not use Claude. The question requires a technique that structures the task for Claude.

Correct. Clustering tickets by topic breaks the large set into manageable sub-problems, enabling focused FAQ generation per cluster. Merging these ensures comprehensive coverage and a well-organized final document.
Incorrect. While summarizing each ticket is a useful preprocessing step, it does not group related issues, so combining summaries still lacks the topic-based organization needed for a coherent FAQ.

Incorrect. Concatenating all tickets and asking Claude to produce the FAQ risks exceeding context limits and lacks structured input, making it difficult to identify recurring themes and organize answers coherently.
